title: Batch & Cache Ops Playlet — explainability audit and micro-tutorial
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and prototype a compact, task-oriented "playlet" inside the Redwood Console that guides operators through safe batching/cache configuration changes. The playlet is a single micro-UX surface combining: 1) an interactive guided tour that applies simulated traffic to preview latency/cost/quality tradeoffs, 2) a transparent explainability audit that surfaces why recommendations are ranked (features, heuristics, historical signals), and 3) inline guardrails with rollback + canary suggestions. Goal: reduce operator uncertainty, avoid risky global changes, and shorten time-to-safe-configuration for Dedicated/Private customers.
user_stories: As an SRE using Redwood Console, I want a quick, opinionated walkthrough that simulates my service's latency/cost impact before I commit batching or cache changes.
As a Platform PM, I want the system to show why a particular recommendation is suggested (e.g., high prefix reuse, KV-cache hit potential), so I can justify it to stakeholders.
As an operator, I want guardrails and a suggested canary rollout so I can minimize customer impact while testing changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playlet prototype in Figma with stepper and simulation panel; 2) Explainability audit card showing top 3 contributing signals for each recommendation; 3) Cost/latency delta estimate computed for small/medium/large workloads; 4) Inline rollback/canary recipe text and copy accepted by content review; 5) Usability test (5 participants) notes and at least 80% of participants can complete simulated change without help.
research_notes: Session-01 (2025-02-18): Ops engineer found the simulation useful but wanted clearer SLO-risk badges
Session-02 (2025-02-21): Product manager requested explicit mapping from recommendation to rollout steps
Heuristic-audit-study: Top signals: prefix-reuse-rate, average-generation-length, previous-cache-hit-rate
design_decisions: Keep playlet minimal—max 4 steps: Analyze -> Recommend -> Simulate -> Apply/Canary
Expose numeric deltas (pct cost, ms p95) with uncertainty bands instead of absolute guarantees
Rank recommendations by composite score: expected-savings * safety-factor; surface the contributing signals in an 'audit bar'.
Disable destructive actions behind a single-confirm modal and default to canary rollout for Dedicated customers.
tradeoffs_considered: Depth vs speed: heavier simulation gives better fidelity but increases time-to-action. Chosen: fast approximate simulation plus optional deep-run.
Transparency vs noise: surfacing too many signals confuses operators. Chosen: top-3 signals + link to full audit log.
Automation vs control: auto-apply could save time but risks regressions. Chosen: recommend + one-click-canary only for users with 'ops' role.
